_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.note: RANKED LAST DELIBERATELY, and it scores 4. Mike's ruling the same day: clear the technical and feature work first so the master team can start UAT testing, THEN double back to wording and document-title alignment. This is wording and title alignment. The pattern is proven and cheap once a name is known — the Seminar seven took five words and a seven-line diff — but each of the 21 needs the REAL page name, and that is Mike's to give, never a developer's to rule on. Put the actual sentences in front of him, not the label: that is what unblocked 2.3 after four sessions. 🔴 A SECOND STEP WAS FOUND ON 2026-08-26 AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Measuring the empty `templates[]` arrays (raised as 4.51, closed the same day) showed that 22 of the branches with an EMPTY array name their templates in the recommendation PROSE instead — "Use Design & Deliver template", "Use De Bono's 6 Hats" — and those prose names are this item's own missing documents, in the same trees (35, cas_, fbp_). The consequence nobody had recorded: `walkLogicTree` in server/utils/logicTrees.js L1037 reads ONLY `node.templates`, never the prose. So the tree's judgement about which tool fits reaches the ADVISER as a sentence and never reaches the RANKING ENGINE, where it is meant to act as the tie-breaker. When the search content is updated and the names resolve, populating `templates[]` on those 22 branches is a required second step — the sentences alone leave the engine exactly as blind as it is now. ⚠ AND IT CANNOT BE DONE FIRST: `validateLogicTreeReferences` scans `nodes[].templates` and hard-fails under VA_STRICT_CONTENT, so writing a name into the array before the document exists turns a silent gap into a broken build.

items.name: Nobody has seen a real conversation's recommendations reach the Team tab
items.why: Merged 2026-07-22 (PR #21, d791a9a): the AI declares its recommendations in a trailing [[TEMPLATES: ...]] marker that the engine holds back from the stream so it never reaches the advisor. THE LIVE CHECK WAS RUN ON 2026-08-26, on Mike laptop, against a live OpenAI key — three complete client conversations driven through to a Phase 3 recommendation, 17 API calls, 77,605 tokens on gpt-4o-mini. Two of the three checks PASSED and are closed. (a) The reply streams normally: the recommendations arrived in 435, 1,094 and 792 separate chunks, token by token. (b) No marker text is ever visible: not one bracket in 2,321 recorded chunks, tested against every partial prefix of the sentinel, against the chunks joined, and against the final rewritten text — and this is not a vacuous pass, because in the succession run the AI demonstrably DID write a marker (its declared order differs from the deterministic prose-scan order, which only the marker preserves) and not one character of it escaped. What remains is (c) alone.
items.risk: Small, and now smaller than it was: the two checks that could show something ugly on screen have both passed. What is still unseen is whether a real session's recommended templates land correctly on the Team tab and set the right capability tier — the record that decides what an advisor is credited with. It cannot go wrong invisibly forever, but nobody has watched it go right once.

So (c) needs any environment with a database, which means UAT rather than a developer machine, and it is a two-minute look: open the Team tab as a firm manager after a real session and check the templates and the tier are the ones the conversation actually produced. ⚠ "Team Dashboard", the name this item used to carry, IS NOT A SCREEN — the words appear nowhere in any page or component, only in a JSDoc comment at tierLookup.js L88. items.name: Meeting Review — slices 1–3 are built; the manager's half remains, and §4 still gates a real recording
items.why: Designed and committed 2026-09-01 (7f5ced1) on Mike's own request: record a client meeting, transcribe it, and produce two reports — a client-facing summary, and an advisor-only review checked against observation points the advisor sets before the meeting and a manager can edit. Five rulings were taken the same day: the advisor alone owns their review and chooses to share it; capture is live in-app; the audio is deleted once a transcript exists, with the transcript on a firm-set clock; it is called Meeting Review; and the advisor's voice is told from the client's by the transcription provider's own diarization, with the advisor identified as whoever speaks the consent line — no stored voice sample, so no biometric data, and no second supplier. SLICE 1 IS BUILT (2026-09-01), on Mike's instruction "build the meeting review feature" and his approval of the screens: the observation points — the platform list, the four-tier cascade through firmOverlay, the mentor-and-firm editing tab, and the advisor's pre-set — 57 new tests, suite green at 6,707, lint 0 errors. SLICE 2 IS ALSO BUILT (2026-09-01), on Mike's instruction "4.56 - slice 2": the retention dial, the two consent screens in the approved words, live capture with a wake-lock and a loud alarm, chunk intake, the whole-recording transcription pass with the speakers separated, and the destruction of the audio — 170 new tests, suite green at 6,880, lint 0 errors. He ruled three things inside it: the audio lives on THIS SERVER'S OWN DISK (never the database, and never the Google Drive pipeline the document library already uses — the consent line promises nothing leaves the firm, and the argument that made OpenAI acceptable does not cover Google); slice 2 TRANSCRIBES as well as captures, because capture without transcription leaves audio with no deletion trigger; and the transcript-EXPIRY job is its own later piece of work. The pre-build check passed and was proven end to end: two synthetic voices, sent as one recording, came back as 8 segments across 2 correctly separated speakers with the consent-reader first. SLICE 3 IS ALSO BUILT (2026-09-02), on Mike's instruction "meeting review reports": the client's Meeting Summary (a draft the advisor edits, approves and copies into their own email), My Coaching Notes (private to the advisor, four measured figures computed in code, one finding per observation point either quoting the transcript or declaring NOT FOUND), the citation check that drops any quote the transcript does not contain, the advisor's disagreement, and the answer on a point a recording cannot hear — 135 new tests, suite green at 7,071 (371 suites), lint 0 errors. He ruled on FOUR things first, each put to him alone, and every one was a place the approved drawing asked for something the code cannot do: "Play this moment" cannot exist because P8 has already destroyed the audio (replaced by showing the surrounding transcript); "Send to client" cannot send because this app has no mail channel and adding one would put client financial content through an unassessed third party (replaced by approve-then-copy); the jargon count is removed because it needs a firm glossary that does not exist and a default word-list would be inventing his content; and whether a point can be heard is marked by its AUTHOR, never judged by the model. WHAT IS NOT BUILT IS THE MANAGER'S HALF: no aggregate above the 5-advisor / 20-meeting threshold, no follow-through check across meetings, no transcript-expiry job, and no firm glossary. Eight decisions were open at filing (Brief §6). ALL THREE BUILD BLOCKERS ARE NOW CLOSED, all on 2026-09-01: speaker separation (provider diarization, advisor anchored to the consent line, no biometric data); the consent wording, approved and registered in design/ARTEFACTS.md under a new 'words a client is told' block — design/MEETING-CONSENT-WORDING.md holds the spoken line, the two-step screen that keeps consent INSIDE the audio rather than before it, and the stop-and-delete path when someone declines or changes their mind; and the PII exception, written into CLAUDE.md, named to this feature, conditional, and explicitly no precedent. What remains before a build is Mike's go — plus a lawyer's review of the wording per market, and the four non-coding items in Brief §4.
items.risk: 🔴 IT HAS CHANGED SHAPE, AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IT IS REAL. Until 2026-09-01 the answer here was "none while it stays on paper". Slice 2 means the code CAN NOW RECORD A CLIENT, and the four items in Brief §4 — a data protection impact assessment, staff consultation, OpenAI's written terms for submitted AUDIO specifically, and a lawyer per market — gate a first real recording rather than a first commit. None of them is a coding task and none is done. The advisor's page carries a banner saying so, WHICH IS A WARNING AND NOT A CONTROL: nothing in the code stops somebody pressing record in front of a client tomorrow. The design's own safeguards are built and tested — consent captured inside the audio, the audio destroyed whether or not transcription succeeded, stop-and-delete taking the transcript with it, a recording readable only by the advisor who made it — but a safeguard is not a permission. The three original blockers are all closed — the wording an advisor speaks to a client is approved and registered, speaker separation is settled without any biometric data, and the PII exception is written into CLAUDE.md with four conditions — but none of those closures removes a build risk, and the exception in particular is a PERMISSION rather than a safeguard: it makes sending a whole client conversation to a model allowed, not safe, and conditions (b) and (d) are the parts a build can quietly fail to honour. The wording still needs a lawyer in each of the eight locales it ships in (Germany treats a secret recording as a criminal matter, not merely a privacy one), and attribution checks that cannot reliably tell who spoke while still reading as confident remain the thing most likely to look fine and be wrong. Brief §4 lists four further things that are nobody's coding task — an impact assessment, staff consultation, the provider's written terms for submitted AUDIO specifically, and the position in each jurisdiction — which is exactly why they are the ones that get discovered late.

items.note: THE BRIEF IS STILL NOT IN design/ARTEFACTS.md, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. That register records what Mike has actually approved. He approved the *writing* of the design, not the design itself, so the Brief has no row — adding one would make the register say something untrue, which is the one thing it exists to prevent. What DOES have a row, from 2026-09-01, is the consent wording, because that he approved outright. The distinction is the whole point of the register: one feature, one approved artefact inside it, and the rest still a proposal. ⚠ THE SECOND REPORT IS THE PRODUCT, AND THE PRE-SET IS WHY IT CAN WORK. Recording and summarising is a commodity; an advisor declaring in advance what the meeting is for is not, and it is also the mechanism that makes the advisor report technically reliable — an open request to grade a person produces confident invention, while a request to find a named thing and quote it or answer NOT FOUND is retrieval with a citation. Any later change that weakens the pre-set (a 'just summarise how it went' mode, say) takes the reliability with it. ⚠ ONE RECOMMENDATION WAS OVERRULED AND THE RESIDUAL RISK IS REAL: upload-a-recording was recommended over live in-app capture and Mike chose live. The failure it does not solve is that an operating system may suspend a backgrounded browser tab, and there is no second take with a real client. Brief P10/P11 contain it; neither eliminates it.

items.name: A point the mentor adds tells a firm manager THEY wrote it
items.why: The observation points carry a source badge — inherited / edited-here / added-here — and it is stamped by whichever level applied decisions. loadResolvedObservations SHORT-CIRCUITS for a scope that has decided nothing, returning the layer above untouched, so the mentor's own added-here stamp travels down intact. A firm manager who has customised nothing therefore sees "Added here" against every point the mentor wrote.
items.risk: It reads as authorship. A firm manager is told they added a point they cannot edit and did not write, which is the opposite of what the badge exists to say — and the badge is what tells them whether a correction of theirs is safe from the mentor's later changes. It looks completely normal on screen, which is why nobody has reported it.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-09-02 while building the meeting TYPES cascade, whose resolver had the identical fault — fixed there, and deliberately NOT patched here, because the points are a shipped screen and their own change. Nobody outside asked; it is filed because a defect we find is still a defect.

items.touches: server/utils/meetingObservations.js (the no-decisions passthrough in loadResolvedObservations) and tests/unit/meetingObservations.test.js. The fix is the one already made in server/utils/meetingTypes.js: restamp the inherited list from the viewer's point of view. Both paths — passthrough and full resolve — must agree, or the badge flickers with unrelated edits.
items.comment: 2026-09-02 — one line plus two assertions, and the fix is already written and proven in the sibling module. Left undone only to keep slice 2 of the types cascade to its approved scope.

items.name: QuickBooks and MYOB are supported on paper, not against a real file
items.why: On 2026-09-02 Mike ruled "Xero" out of every user-facing string in favour of "your accounting software", then asked for the reader to be tested against QuickBooks and MYOB. It was — against RECONSTRUCTIONS of each package's published report layout, because no real export from either exists on this machine. That found five genuine defects, all fixed: the "As of" date line was never read; header rows were walked as body rows; the company name sits ABOVE the title in both packages and below it in Xero, so the scan took the first section heading as the company and lost that whole section; QuickBooks' "LIABILITIES AND EQUITY" heading made every liability under it read as equity (a defect introduced the same morning in 659706d); and MYOB lists bank accounts with no "Bank" heading. server/report/intake/supportedPackages.js now marks Xero `verified` and the other two `expected`, and every screen says which is which. WHAT REMAINS IS FOUR FILES: a real Balance Sheet and a real Profit and Loss exported from QuickBooks Online, and the same two from MYOB.
items.risk: The app now names three packages it can read, and two of them have never had a real file put through them. A reconstruction proves the reader copes with the layout as documented; it cannot prove the layout is right, and a real chart of accounts is the thing that surprises you — reading the real Xero exports on 2026-07-13 and 2026-07-15 refuted three assumptions outright. The exposure is contained rather than absent: every intake screen says the two are not yet confirmed and asks the advisor to check the figures, and every seeded figure is tagged by its source. But a wrong opening balance that looks plausible is exactly what a person in UAT cannot catch, and it would reach a client's forecast.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-02 — "keep it as a job for future - keep moving forward", after being told that four real exports are what would move the two packages from `expected` to `verified`.

items.touches: Nothing until the files arrive. Then: tests/unit/accountingPackages.test.js (the reconstructions become real-shaped fixtures), server/report/intake/xeroReportParser.js if the real layouts differ, and server/report/intake/supportedPackages.js to flip each `confidence` to `verified` — which its own guard will not allow until the evidence line says a real export was read.
items.comment: 2026-09-02 — filed on Mike's instruction. NOTHING IS BLOCKED: the reader handles both layouts today and the screens are honest about the difference. DO NOT PROMOTE ON MORE RECONSTRUCTIONS — the guard in accountingPackages.test.js fails the build if a package is marked `verified` without evidence naming a real export, and that is deliberate.

items.name: The forecast reads one year and one file — the volatility read and the two-year trend remain
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: drop the last two years of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet so basic trend analysis can be performed, including volatility. IT IS TWO SEPARATE PIECES AND ONE OF THEM IS ALREADY BUILT. (a) VOLATILITY NEEDS MONTHS, NOT YEARS — server/report/volatilityModel.js takes 24 MONTHLY sales figures, so two annual P&Ls give it two data points and no variation can be measured from two points. What feeds it is the by-month export, and Mike's own ruling of 2026-08-31 ("two files, up to 24 months") is built as server/report/intake/monthlySeriesAssembler.js, which joins this year's and last year's by-month exports, warns on gaps and overlaps, and strips the incomplete trailing months. The Volatility model, page, report component and intake route are all live. 🔴 PHASE (a) — THE FILE CONNECTION — IS BUILT (2026-09-03). Step 1 now offers FOUR slots, this year's and last year's by-month exports named separately, and the route passes both to `assembleMonthlySeries`, which has accepted two files since it was written. Mike approved the scope and the wording before a line was changed. THE REASON IT MATTERS turned out to be sharper than 'more months': a current-year export almost always stops part-way through a month, those trailing months are stripped as incomplete, so ONE file can yield eleven usable months and NO SEED AT ALL — the advisor then types twelve months of sales by hand and nothing on screen says why. Pinned by a test that runs the same mid-year export twice, alone and with last year's beside it. One pre-existing defect was found and fixed in passing, with his approval: `TOO_MANY_MONTHLY_FILES` was never on the allowlist in server/report/intakeError.js, so that refusal's authored sentence had been replaced by a generic one since the day it was written. WHAT REMAINS OF (a) is the volatility read itself — handing the same 24 months to the built volatility engine and showing it on the forecast. Mike asked for it on 2026-09-03; it puts a new block on a screen he has already approved, so it needs its own drawing and his word before it is built. (b) THE TREND READ IS GENUINELY NEW WORK. Two years of ANNUAL accounts gives what volatility cannot: growth, margin movement, and whether debtor, creditor and stock days are improving. It is blocked on one specific thing — xeroReportParser.js L70-79 REFUSES a multi-column export outright (MULTI_PERIOD_COLUMNS) and, where the columns are few, reads only the first and warns. A comparative Balance Sheet with this year beside last year is exactly that shape, so today it either bounces or silently reads one year. That guard is deliberate and must not be weakened; the fix is to teach the parser to read columns as periods when it is asked to.
items.risk: Nothing is broken while this is undone, and that is the point — the forecast is honest about reading one period. The risk is in the doing. The comparative-column work touches the guard that stops a two-year file being read as one, and that guard exists because a figure from the wrong year is completely believable; weakening it to accept two years would be the single easiest way to produce a confident wrong opening position. The volatility connection carries the join risk the assembler already names: two by-month exports read separately are two correct halves, joined wrongly they are one confident wrong series.

items.name: Economic analysis — the forecast asks the AI for market research, because the forecasts support funding requests
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: a tick on the Three-Way Forecast reading "economic analysis", which charges the AI to conduct global and local market research so it can be included in an overall report — "since the majority of 3 way forecasts are used to support funding requests". He will supply the detailed instructions and the prompt himself. 🔴 WHAT MAKES IT LARGER THAN A TICK, AND IT IS NOT A CODING PREFERENCE: it would be the FIRST report model in this app to call the AI. server/routes/report.js never touches OpenAI today — only server/routes/cases.js does — and every one of the Report-class models is pure maths to screen. Four consequences follow. (a) THE PROMPT HAS A HOME ALREADY: the AI Prompts hub page (built 2026-08-22, item 4.28) holds the cash-flow forecast prompt as locked-body-with-editable-variables in data/ai-prompts.json, and that page exists precisely so a firm can tune the named variables without a developer — Mike's prompt belongs there, not hardcoded in a prompt builder, which is also what the hub-page rule requires. (b) THE FLAGGED ISSUES REGISTER COMES BACK: it was deferred in the AI Prompts design under Q4 for one stated reason — "it is an approval workflow for AI output, and no report calls the AI yet" — and that deferral expires the moment a report does. (c) IT CANNOT RUN INLINE: the engineering standard caps a page-render backend response at 2000 ms and otherwise requires a job id and polling. Market research will take far longer, so it is a job, and the screen has to say so rather than appear to hang. (d) THE PROVENANCE SYSTEM NEEDS A FOURTH STATE: the forecast already tags every figure `file`, `entered` or `seeded`, and AI-sourced commentary needs its own tag so nobody mistakes a model's assertion about a market for a figure read from the client's accounts.
items.risk: AI text going into a document a bank reads. The standards already require an explicit `isApproved: true` before AI output is committed for financial work, and "never trust LLM output as structured data" bites with unusual force here: a confident and wrong claim about a market, sitting inside a funding pack, is exactly the failure a person in UAT cannot catch, because it looks exactly like research. 🔴 PRIVACY NEEDS A FRESH RULING FROM MIKE AND MUST NOT BE INFERRED. Useful market research needs the client's industry and location, and "specialist importer of X in Nelson" identifies a business in a small market as surely as a name does. The standing rule is to strip internal DB IDs and PII before anything reaches an LLM; the ONE exception granted so far — Meeting Review, 2026-09-01 — was written into CLAUDE.md as conditional and "explicitly no precedent", and it says in terms that another feature wanting to send personal data to a model is a fresh decision for Mike. This is that fresh decision.

items.name: International vs local — the forecast treats every sale and every purchase as domestic
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: an international-versus-local split for purchases AND sales on step 3, so imported stock that takes longer to arrive and needs deposits can be entered, as can overseas sales that are only paid after delivery — allowing for shipping and FX. 🔴 IT BUYS MORE THAN THE TIMING HE ASKED FOR, AND THE SECOND GAIN IS THE LARGER ONE. (a) TIMING, partly expressible today: the five collection buckets already stretch to "four months after", but there is ONE BLENDED PROFILE for everything, so a firm 70% local paid in 30 days and 30% export paid in 120 has to average two different behaviours into a single curve — which averages away exactly the thing that matters. A split gives each stream its own profile, on both sides. (b) 🔴 GST, WHICH THE MODEL CANNOT EXPRESS AT ALL TODAY — checked in the engine, not assumed: `gstOnIncome` applies GST to EVERY sale and `gstOnExpenses` applies it to EVERY purchase on the same schedule. Exports are typically ZERO-RATED, so no GST output arises at all; imports pay GST AT THE BORDER on landed cost, when the goods clear customs, not when the supplier's balance is paid. So for an importer-exporter today's GST schedule is wrong in both directions at once. That is not a rounding matter: GST is a cash payment on a fixed filing cycle, which is the whole reason R5 (the six-monthly return returning #REF! in month one) mattered. THE COST, honestly: the engine grows a second sales series, a second purchase series and two more profiles, so step 3 goes from two collection cards to four on the densest of the four screens — hence the recommendation to put the international set behind a tick ("Does this business buy or sell overseas?") so the majority who trade only locally see what they see today.
items.risk: 🔴 THE ONE SAFEGUARD THIS ITEM MUST NOT BE BUILT WITHOUT: if both international series default to zero and their profiles are ignored when empty, the 10,155-cell golden test MUST produce byte-identical output. That test is written FIRST, before any of the rest — it is the only thing that proves Mike's workbook port is untouched by the addition, and this change reaches into the GST computation, which the golden set covers cell by cell. Beyond it: the engine currently derives cost of goods from a single mark-up percentage, and import margins usually differ from domestic, so the international stream probably wants its own — a ruling for Mike inside the drawing, not a developer's call. And the failure mode if the GST half is got wrong is the believable kind: a zero-rated export wrongly charged GST, or border GST landing in the month the supplier is paid rather than the month the goods clear, moves real cash between months in a schedule nobody re-checks.

items.name: Overseas stock purchases — the Import & Retail model feeds the forecast
items.why: Mike's request, 2026-09-03: read the Import & Retail model he loaded and see how future overseas stock purchases could be included in the Three-Way Forecast, as a future building phase. THE WORKBOOK IS NOW IN THE REPO — design/report-source-models/Import & Retail.xlsx, copied on his approval (8b550fe), byte-identical to his own, and read end to end with the repo's own xlsxReader. Five sheets: two supplier input sheets (plus a copy of one), an Index Tables lookup and Financial Projections. Each supplier sheet turns a short input set into a payment schedule — manufacture days 120, order balance due 91, pre-retail prep 9; deposit 60%, interest cover 6%, currency movement 10%; 20 stock lines each with a unit cost and a demand pattern (SkyRockets / Steady Eddy / Slow Burn); container size, shipping speed, count, refrigerated surcharge — yielding 4,469 units, 693,271 of unit cost, a 415,963 deposit and 255,650 balance due across twelve 30-day bands, with balance interest and FX loss computed separately. Index Tables holds the sell-through curves: the proportion of a line sold in each 30-day band, per demand pattern. Financial Projections is the monthly schedule — wages, deposit payments, balance payments, shipping, total payments, projected revenue, import-related monthly cash movement, opening and closing balance, with Peak / Off Peak / Normal seasonality. 🔴 THE ARCHITECTURE IS SETTLED IN PRINCIPLE AND IT IS THE CHEAP ONE: this is an UPSTREAM CALCULATOR, not a section inside the forecast. It generates two inputs the forecast ALREADY takes — the twelve monthly `purchases` and the twelve monthly `sales` — so the forecast engine needs no new arithmetic at all.
items.risk: Four questions have to be ruled before a line is written, and the first is the dangerous one. (1) THE IMPORT MODEL WORKS IN 30-DAY BANDS AND THE FORECAST WORKS IN CALENDAR MONTHS. Mike's own R9 ruling of 2026-09-02 — "obviously, it needs to be per calendar month" — exists because 31-day stepping ran three weeks adrift over three years and misfiled the GST schedule. Joining a 30-day series to a calendar-month one is exactly that class of error, and a payment landing in the wrong month is completely believable. (2) THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT FX LOSS: the import model computes currency movement and balance interest as separate figures and the forecast has no such line — the nearest homes are a direct-cost line or an overhead, and that is Mike's call. (3) TWO ROUTES TO COST OF GOODS: the forecast derives cost from the mark-up percentage, the import model has real unit costs per stock line. One has to win, or they have to be reconciled — and whichever loses is silently overridden, which is the failure nobody sees. (4) The deposit is paid roughly 220 days before the first sale, which IS the working-capital hole a funding request exists to cover, so the timing has to be right for the feature to be worth anything.

items.name: The book value of one asset is typed, because no screen ever asks for the Fixed Asset Schedule
items.why: Selling an asset on the Three-Way Forecast needs two figures — the price, and the book value it is carried at — because the gain or loss between them is profit in the month of the sale (correction R10, 2026-09-03). THE APP CANNOT DERIVE THE SECOND ONE, and the reason is structural rather than an omission: it holds SIX CATEGORY TOTALS, seeded from Balance Sheet line names in server/report/intake/xeroReportParser.js L290-296, so it knows "Motor Vehicles 80,000" and can never know that 8,000 of it is the 2019 Hilux. That is the workbook's own structure, not a gap in the port. 🔴 MIKE IS RIGHT THAT THE FIGURE EXISTS — his words: "if i have a vehicle it must be listed in the asset schedule and balance sheet - which is paired to the depreciation rates - cant see why you cant pull the book value from that?" It does exist, in the FIXED ASSET SCHEDULE, which is a different report from the Balance Sheet and which step 1 has never asked for. Step 1 takes a Balance Sheet, a Profit and Loss, and up to two by-month P&Ls. Reading a fifth would turn a Sell row into picking the actual asset off a list, with its book value and its depreciation rate already attached.
items.risk: Nothing is broken while this is undone — the advisor reads the number off the same schedule the app would otherwise parse, and the arithmetic is identical either way. The risk is in the DOING, and it is the one already on the board at 4.60: a Fixed Asset Schedule varies far more between accounting packages than a Balance Sheet does, and this repository currently supports three packages of which only Xero has ever had a real export put through it. Adding a second unverified reader on top of the first is how two paper-supported packages become four. There is also a quieter failure available: a schedule read wrongly gives a book value that looks entirely plausible, and a wrong book value moves the gain, the tax and the retained earnings together, so nothing on screen looks odd.
